H., Firat, O., Auli, M., Ruder, S., Riesa, J., & Johnson, M. (2022). XTREME-S: Evaluating Cross-lingual Speech Representations. arXiv preprint arXiv:2203.10752.
creator: Alexis Conneau, Ankur Bapna, Yu Zhang, Min Ma, Patrick von Platen, Anton Lozhkov, Colin Cherry, Ye Jia, Clara Rivera, Mihir Kale, Daan Van Esch, Vera Axelrod, Simran Khanuja, Jonathan H. Clark, Orhan Firat, Michael Auli, Sebastian Ruder, Jason Riesa, Melvin Johnson (Google Research, Hugging Face, Meta AI)
description: XTREME-S is a benchmark to evaluate universal cross-lingual speech representations in 102 languages. It covers four task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation, and retrieval.
name: XTREME-S
rai:annotationsPerItem: between one and three recordings for each sentence (2.3 on average)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For the Fleurs dataset, 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest sets were used. Between one and three recordings were collected for each sentence. Speakers of the train sets are different than speakers from the dev/test sets.
rai:dataCollection: XTREME-S aggregates several existing datasets (MLS, VoxPopuli, CoVoST-2, Minds-14) and introduces a new dataset, Fleurs. For Fleurs, 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest sets were used, and between one and three recordings were collected for each sentence in 102 languages.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Read audiobooks (LibriVox), European Parliament sessions, e-banking domain spoken data, and read speech of Wikipedia/FLoRes sentences.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For Minds-14, monolingual datasets are merged into a single multilingual dataset, with a 30-20-50% train-dev-test split. For Fleurs, new train-dev-test splits are built with 1509, 150, and 350 sentences respectively.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Some slight improvements and changes may be done in a 2nd version of the dataset (e.g. missing recordings, or replaced low-quality recordings). Updates will be made on our platform.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Making speech technology available in all languages is especially important to give speakers of under-represented languages an equal voice on the Internet, and the possibility to make their content and culture known outside of their language cluster.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating universal cross-lingual speech representations across speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation, and retrieval tasks.
